ordered_diagnoses: Undifferentiated embryonal sarcoma of the liver

s1.syndrome_frame: Abdominal pain with liver dysfunction and a large cystic liver tumor
salient_findings: Elevated alkaline phosphatase and γ-glutamyl transferase
Large cystic liver tumor with solid components
key_facts: Negative hepatitis B and C viral markers
Normal α-fetoprotein, PIVKA-II, CEA, and CA19-9 levels
Abdominal CT showed a 16 cm cystic tumor in the liver
MRI showed mixed high and low signal intensity
Abdominal ultrasound demonstrated a honeycomb-like tumor
PET–CT showed FDG uptake in the solid components of the cyst

shortlist: Undifferentiated embryonal sarcoma of the liver

shortlist.label: Mucinous cystadenocarcinoma of the liver
shortlist.why_kept: Imaging findings of a cystic tumor with solid components and elevated DUPAN-2 and CA125 levels are consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Biliary cystadenocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Similar imaging characteristics and the presence of a large cystic tumor in the liver make this a plausible diagnosis

shortlist.label: Hepatic sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: The presence of a large, heterogeneous, multilocular cystic tumor with solid components and FDG uptake on PET-CT is consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: The location and appearance of the tumor, as well as the patient's age and liver function tests, make this a possible diagnosis

shortlist.label: Undifferentiated embryonal sarcoma of the liver
shortlist.why_kept: The presence of a large, aggressive-appearing tumor with mixed solid and cystic components makes this a rare but possible diagnosis

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with a large cystic liver tumor, elevated DUPAN-2 and CA125 levels, and imaging findings of a multilocular cystic tumor with solid components and intratumoral hemorrhage are consistent with mucinous cystadenocarcinoma of the liver

rejected.label: Biliary cystadenocarcinoma
rejected.why: While similar, biliary cystadenocarcinoma typically presents with more prominent biliary obstruction symptoms and is less likely to have the specific tumor marker elevations seen in this case

rejected.label: Hepatic sarcoma
rejected.why: Hepatic sarcoma is a rare tumor that does not typically present with the cystic and solid components seen on imaging in this case

rejected.label: Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma
rejected.why: Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma usually presents as a solid mass rather than a cystic tumor and is less likely to have the tumor marker profile seen in this patient

rejected.label: Undifferentiated embryonal sarcoma of the liver
rejected.why: This rare tumor typically occurs in children and young adults, and the imaging and laboratory findings in this case do not support this diagnosis
